title: Chapter 135: Bottom of the Well
html:
When a scream erupted from Mu Yang High School, Chen Ge opened the boards and hurried inside. This was the scenario’s first public trial, and he feared the mannequins might go too far.

They already took Chen Yalin’s name tag from the entrance. Didn’t they suspect a trap? Hopefully, carrying it won’t pressure the Pen Spirit into doing anything foolish.

At the sealed classroom, he found a mannequin on the floor clutching its own head. It seemed to be trying to reattach it but could not locate the proper position.

Why is she outside?Inside, desks lay in disarray and several mannequins had lost their heads. Judging by this mess, the visitors were terrified. They wouldn’t have deliberately carried her out.

Chen Ge propped her against the wall and reattached her head. When he met the mannequin’s gaze, something seemed to live behind its eyes. He could almost sense shyness and respect.

He searched every page of the black phone but found no option for controlling the lingering spirits. Instead, he told the mannequin, “You may leave the classroom, but you cannot leave Mu Yang High School. Understood?”

She gave no response. Whether she understood or not, Chen Ge left her against the corridor wall and entered the classroom to reset the others.

They found three of the four tags. This group isn’t bad.As he worked, his foot struck something beneath the center desk. Why is there a phone here?

…

“Did anyone hear voices behind us?” Pei Hu’s legs trembled, and he looked over his shoulder every few steps. Even Xia Meili had grown tired of his cowardice.

“Poor kitty, if you’re that afraid, just stay here and wait for us to come back.”

“Who are you calling a kitty? Meili, you didn’t see what happened. The room was so dark that I needed my phone’s flashlight. While I was untying the knot, the mannequin’s head creaked and turned toward me.” Even the memory frightened Pei Hu. He gestured wildly, then reached into his pocket and gasped. “F*ck! I was so focused on the name tag that I left my phone behind!”

“Then go get it. Why are you telling me?” Xia Meili shot him a sidelong look.

“You expect me to go back alone?” Pei Hu stared miserably into the corridor, which resembled a monster’s open jaws. “Forget it. I’ll ask an employee to retrieve it after we leave.”

He ran after the rest of the group, and the five stopped at the first junction.

“How large is this place? The path splits, and neither corridor has an end in sight.” Pei Hu squeezed beside Wang Hailong. “Brother Long, we can still turn back.”

“Get off me.” Wang Hailong was nervous too, but would not reveal it before Dou Menglu. “A third of our time is gone, and we still need twenty tags. Five people together are too slow. Wenlong and Pei Hu can take the left corridor; I’ll take Menglu and Meili to the right.”

“We have no issue with that,” the two girls said.

“Fine with me,” Wang Wenlong said confidently. “Even if we fail, we’ll have mapped the scenario for our friend’s attempt.”

“Then it’s decided. The two of you’d better stick close to me.” Wang Hailong led the two girls down the corridor that led to the girls’ dormitory.

“F*ck! Does no one care what I think?”

“Come on, Pei Hu. You’re with me.” Wang Wenlong set off. Pei Hu reluctantly followed; being left alone would be worse.

“There doesn’t seem to be anything scary here.”

At the end of the passage, Wang Wenlong and Pei Hu exchanged startled looks. The corridor divided again.

One narrow path ended at an old well; the other led to a door numbered 303.

“Let’s go together.” Pei Hu grabbed Wang Wenlong’s arm tightly.

“Okay.” Wang Wenlong looked into the distance. “Why do you think there’s a well at the end of the road?”

“An actor playing a ghost probably hides in there.”

“Probably. The owner likes hiding tags in frightening places, so there must be at least one inside the well.” Wang Wenlong sounded certain. “Let’s look.”

They peered into the two-meter-deep shaft. Wang Wenlong aimed his phone’s light downward and, as expected, found two name tags at the bottom.

“This is too easy.” Pei Hu took a step back. Jumping into the well to take the nametags was definitely not something he would do.

“Be careful. Nothing frightened us on the way here, so the well must contain a trap.” Wang Wenlong swept his flashlight across every surface but found nothing unusual. It looked like an ordinary old well.

“Did I overestimate him?” Wang Wenlong relaxed. With so many tags to hide, creating a trap for each would be impossible.

He passed the phone to Pei Hu. “You stay above the well and hold the light for me. I’ll go into the well to collect the nametags.”

“Okay.” Pei Hu sighed with relief. Anything was acceptable as long as he stayed aboveground; with his size, squeezing into the well would be difficult anyway.

Wang Wenlong was slight but athletic, as though he trained daily. “Pei Hu, if you run away while I’m down there, I’ll skin you alive when we get out.”

“What kind of man do you think I am? I would never do that.” Pei Hu looked offended. “You all underestimate me. I’ll prove it.”

Before he finished, Wang Wenlong jumped into the well.

From inside, the dark well seemed much deeper. “Is it my imagination, or did the shaft just grow?”

A layer of sand cushioned his landing. “I was right. The owner expects visitors to jump down here; otherwise, he wouldn’t have padded the bottom.”

He examined the walls. Some patches were slick, while others bore claw marks left by something that seemed to have been buried alive and fought to escape.

“This is unsettling.” Wang Wenlong looked up and felt the mouth of the well recede farther above him.
